BlackRock's Hambro blasts gold miners' ‘reckless capital allocation towards share buybacks
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – BlackRock, the world’s largest asset manager, sees the recent spate of share buybacks by gold miners as reckless and undisciplined, and believes that with gold prices likely to rise higher, the miners and their shareholders would be far better served by investing in new production. Evy Hambro, global head of thematic and sector investing at BlackRock, said at the FT Mining Summit this week that the share buyback programmes amount to “reckless capital allocation,” and that gold companies were approving these repurchases “without any real process.” “One of the things we’ve been really dismayed about in the last 18 months or so has been the reckless capital allocation towards share buybacks in gold companies, where we’ve seen enormous amounts of money deployed on buybacks without any real process,” he said.

Gold holds near $4,170 as inflation keeps December Fed tightening in play - Kitco AM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) – Spot gold prices were near steady and spot silver prices were modestly higher in early U.S. trading Friday, as a softer dollar and lower Treasury yields on the week continued to support precious metals following Thursday's rebound. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh refrained from signaling an October rate increase during overnight remarks at the International Monetary Fund meetings, reducing immediate tightening expectations despite persistent inflation pressure. At the time of writing, spot gold was trading near $4,172.10 an ounce, up $2.30, or 0.06%, while spot silver was trading near $57.630, up $0.330, or 0.57%. Market positioning remains divided between stubborn inflation and growing concerns about economic resilience. September CPI rose 0.6% on the month and 3.7% annually , while Thursday's producer-price report showed a 1.3% monthly increase and a 6.3% annual gain , the largest monthly rise since March 2022. Producer energy prices jumped 10.8%, adding to concerns that elevated crude and fuel costs could prolong inflation. September retail sales increased 0.8% , suggesting consumer demand remains resilient, while initial jobless claims rose slightly to 199,000. The inflation data have kept December Federal Reserve tightening expectations elevated, but near-term rate pricing has shifted considerably. Following Warsh's remarks in Bangkok, traders reduced the probability of an October rate hike to roughly 15%, while the probability of a December increase remained near 89%. The 10-year Treasury yield was trading near 5.11%, down approximately 14 basis points on the week, as concerns about debt-financed artificial intelligence investment helped fuel demand for government bonds. The dollar index retreated toward 101.9, easing another source of pressure on bullion.
